answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a violet as the anchor of the cost.
